questions.q: Which compound does NOT give effervescence of H₂ with a freshly cut piece of sodium?
questions.explain: Diethyl ether has no acidic hydrogen that sodium can replace. Alcohols, phenols and terminal alkynes all form sodium salts and release hydrogen.

questions.q: 0.2 mol of dry ethanol is treated with excess sodium metal. How many moles of H₂ are evolved?
questions.explain: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂, so 2 mol of alcohol give 1 mol of H₂; 0.2 mol gives 0.1 mol.

questions.q: Why must the sample and test tube be completely dry for the sodium metal test?
options: Moisture converts sodium into sodium peroxide
Water dissolves the sodium alkoxide and hides the result
Water also reacts with sodium to give H₂, causing a false positive
questions.explain: Water reacts with sodium even faster than alcohols and also liberates hydrogen, so a wet sample would give effervescence regardless of the compound.

questions.q: Sodium metal can be used to distinguish which pair of compounds?
questions.explain: These functional isomers (both C₄H₁₀O) differ in acidic hydrogen: the alcohol gives H₂, the ether does not. In the other pairs both members give the same result.
